text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-89234 fired — metering-ingest lag / token delta backlog (severity: P1). Alert: consumer-group 'usage-ingest-main' falling behind, ~18M token delta in the last 30m. Possible invoice risk.
PagerDuty: PD-89234 created and routed to @Elaine (oncall). Escalation policy: 10m -> oncall -> eng-sre.
Elaine (oncall): Acked. I'm on it, pulling logs now.
Jamal: I can help with ingestion side, paging in. Is this consumer a new deploy?
Sofia: Not a deploy AFAIK, we had a small GC spike on nodes earlier but everything was green after.
Matt: Noted. I'll check the Kafka lag metrics and consumer liveness.
Billing Ops: Heads up — if this keeps >4 hours invoices for 2024-07 customers could be affected. We might need to hold invoices.
Elaine (oncall): Command I'm running: `kubectl logs -n metering deploy/usage-ingest-main --since=30m | gzip -c | tail -n 200` to see errors.
SRE-Bot: consumer-group lag summary: partitions with lag > 100k: 12, total lag tokens ~18,430,112. Latest checkpoint stalled at offset 1452309873.
Elaine (oncall): I'm seeing repeated `ERR: checkpoint commit timeout` and `Error: consumer heartbeat not acked`. Looks like commit flaps.
Jamal: Could be DB writeback stall for checkpoints. Which writer is used? `metering-checkpoint-writer-v2`. I can ssh to the writer.
Sofia: Also seeing a spike in RPS to the checkpoints service around 19:14 UTC — maybe a retry loop.
Elaine (oncall): Reached out to `metering-checkpoint-writer` pod logs: `deadline exceeded writing checkpoint -> retry` in a tight loop. CPU not high, but DB connection pool exhaustion visible in logs.
Matt: Opening the DB pool dashboard now. If connections are exhausted, new consumers can't commit which makes them reprocess and pile up lag.
Finance Lead: How many customers are currently in the 0-24h window that would see incorrect token counts? Please approximate so we can assess invoice risk.
Billing Ops: Quick look: ~450 customers with daily billing across affected partitions; ~30 customers with high volume (>1M tokens/day). Risk: high for the latter group.
Elaine (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) scale up checkpoint writer replicas x2 immediately, 2) bump DB pool size, 3) enable temporary backlog throttle (drop non-essential debug telemetry) to reduce write pressure. Implementing step 1 now.
Jamal: On it, `kubectl scale deploy/metering-checkpoint-writer-v2 --replicas=4 -n metering` — running.
SRE-Bot: Scale command accepted. New pods pending.
Elaine (oncall): Step 2: editing configmap `metering-db` to bump pool_max from 50 -> 120 and cycling writer pods. Applying: `kubectl apply -f metering-db-configmap.yaml` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/metering-checkpoint-writer-v2`.
Sofia: Heads up: increasing DB pool may hit the DB tier. Matt, are read replicas healthy?
Matt: Primary is at 68% CPU, connections at 94/100 — we can accept a temporary bump but won't exceed 150 connections. Keep me posted, I'll watch for slow queries.
Elaine (oncall): Rolling restart started. Observing pod readiness.
SRE-Bot: New writer pods ready in 90s. Checkpoint commits per second increased from 12 -> 220. Consumer lag drop beginning at 19:33 UTC.
Jamal: Nice. Lag trending down: 18.4M -> 4.2M in 20m.
Billing Ops: Progress noted. At current slope invoices likely safe if we sustain for next 2h. Still monitoring high-volume customers.
PagerDuty: PD-89234 acknowledged by Elaine (oncall).
Finance Lead: If this stays under 2M token delta in next hour, we can avoid manual invoice holds. Please ping if trend reverses.
Elaine (oncall): Setting a watch and alert: add a temporary threshold — if total lag > 3M again, re-alert and escalate to eng-sre.
SRE-Bot: New temporary alert rule added: `metering.ingest.total_token_lag > 3000000` -> notify incidents.
Sofia: Quick postmortem notes for later: root suspected: checkpoint writer DB pool misconfiguration + retry amplification. Need rate-limiter for checkpoint commits and circuit-breaker on DB errors.
Matt: Also plan to add a consumer-side backoff to avoid hot-retries when commit fails.
Elaine (oncall): Immediate customer comms: Billing Ops, can you draft a short note for impacted high-volume customers if we need to hold invoices? Keep it ready but don't send yet.
Billing Ops: Drafting now, will share in #billing-prodsupport.
Jamal: Follow-up actions I'm taking: 1) file an incident with root-cause label `checkpoint-db-pool-exhaustion`, 2) open PR to add commit-rate limiter, 3) schedule runbook update.
Elaine (oncall): Thanks. Running a full consumer rebalance to expedite progress: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --group usage-ingest-main --reset-offsets --to-latest --execute` executed carefully to avoid duplicate processing — note: doing windowed small restarts to avoid write storms.
SRE-Bot: After rebalance, lag now 1.1M total.
Billing Ops: Good news — high-volume customers now below risk threshold. Finance Lead, recommend no invoice holds at this time.
Finance Lead: Agreed. Keep me updated; we will expect a write-up within 24h for audit.
Elaine (oncall): Closing timeline: PD fired 19:08 UTC, mitigations applied 19:20-19:35, steady recovery 19:36 onwards. Leaving incident open for postmortem.
Jamal: Adding logs and metrics snapshot to the incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-89234 (will attach exported graphs).
Sofia: Adding runbook note: add DB pool sanity check to deploy-time tests.
Elaine (oncall): Any objections to moving to incident -> postmortem state in 2h? We should let the system stabilize.
Matt: Fine with that. I'll keep watch on DB connections for the next 3h.
Billing Ops: We'll keep customer comms on standby.
Incident Bot: PD-89234 status: acknowledged. Incident will be updated when postmortem is filed. :white_check_mark:
Elaine (oncall): Thanks team, marking this thread for follow-up.
